title: Heaven and its Wonders and Hell
author: Emanuel Swedenborg
description: Heaven and its Wonders and Hell, from Things Heard and Seen (De Caelo et ejus Mirabilibus et de Inferno, London, 1758) by Emanuel Swedenborg (1688-1772), the Swedish scientist and visionary, in English translation. Swedenborg's most widely read work, it describes the spiritual world he claimed to have visited over many years. In 603 numbered sections it explains that God is visible in heaven as the spiritual sun of divine love, that heaven has the form of one 'Grand Man', the correspondences between spiritual and natural things, the life, homes, work, language and marriages of angels, the world of spirits where people go after death, the human being's state after death, and the nature of hell, which people choose according to their ruling love; freedom depends on the equilibrium between heaven and hell. It influenced Blake, Emerson, Balzac, Spiritualism and the doctrine of correspondences across later esotericism.
